page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. The configuration provides 12 vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with 1 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, as measured by stress-ng, falls into the bottom 10% tier, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core execution scales effectively, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core scoring 11354.0, and Passmark CPU scoring 22472.2 all registering in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is consistent, achieving 60.68 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 40.05 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, also perform within average parameters.

This instance offers a highly cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. The shared CPU model allows for a high vCPU count at a lower resource cost, making it suitable for parallelizable tasks like software compilation, multi-threaded text processing, and static web serving. Conversely, it is poorly suited for single-threaded applications or demanding real-time tasks like medium-scale LLM text generation, where it performs in the bottom 10%. It is best deployed for development environments, CI/CD pipelines, and distributed background processing.
